record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
record.context_brief: effect algebra sharp, block, and center substructures
record.original_question: An effect algebra is a partial algebra (E; ⊕, 0, 1) with distinct 0 and 1 and a partially defined binary operation ⊕ satisfying commutativity when a ⊕ b is defined, associativity when one side is defined, the existence for every a in E of a unique b with a ⊕ b = 1, and the condition that if 1 ⊕ a is defined then a = 0. Define a <= b iff there is c in E such that a ⊕ c = b; call E a lattice effect algebra or complete effect algebra when (E, <=) is respectively a lattice or complete lattice. Define a <-> b iff a∨b = a⊕(b⊖(a∧b)), let a block B be a maximal subset of E whose elements are pairwise related by <->, set S(E) = {x in E | x ∧ x' = 0}, B(E) = ⋂{B subset E | B is a block of E}, and C(E) = S(E) ∩ B(E). Describe all lattice effect algebras, and all complete lattice effect algebras, satisfying each of the following properties: C(E) = S(E), C(E) = B(E), and C(E) = S(E) = B(E).

evidence.quote: A partial algebra (E; ⊕, 0, 1) is called an effect algebra if 0, 1 are two distinct elements and ⊕ is a partially defined binary operation on E.
If (E, <=) is a lattice (complete lattice) then E is called a lattice effect algebra (complete effect algebra).
Problem 12.1. Describe the family of all lattice (complete) effect algebras with one of the following properties: C(E) = S(E), C(E) = B(E), C(E) = S(E) = B(E).

artifact.status_search_result: Related structural results on centers, sharp elements, and blocks of lattice effect algebras exist (e.g., the identity $C(E)=B(E)\cap S(E)$, atomicity consequences when $C(E)=S(E)$, and block decomposition results). However, a complete classification/description of all lattice (and complete lattice) effect algebras satisfying the three coincidence conditions does not appear to be established in the literature found, so the status of the problem remains unclear.

status_evidence.title: Atomicity of lattice effect algebras and their sub-lattice effect algebras
status_evidence.snippet: S(E) is an orthomodular lattice; C(E)=B(E)∩S(E); when C(E)=S(E), C(E) is atomic and every block is atomic.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural results are known but no full description of the classes.

status_evidence.title: The block structure of complete lattice ordered effect algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies block decomposition of complete lattice effect algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Block structure is studied but not under the specific equalities C(E)=S(E)=B(E).
